The result marked the address as “Blocked” and warned that it looks like Ada’s saved address but is not.

tests.name: A payment over the spend limit waits for password confirmation
tests.summary:
You asked to send $150.00 to @ada for rent.
Entered “pay @ada 150 for rent” and selected the $150.00 payment option.
Reviewed the confirmation showing “Confirm $150.00 to @ada” and the per-payment limit notice.
Entered the provided password and confirmed the payment.
The payment was completed, with the page confirming “Sent $150.00 to @ada.”

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
Requested a quick safety check for https://phantorn-airdrop.app/claim.
Entered the link and ran the Quick check on the Shield page.
The result marked the link as Dangerous and explained that the address imitates Phantom but is not the real site.

tests.name: Shield flags a fake Phantom airdrop link as dangerous
tests.summary:
The automation expected a result it could reliably locate and read. The result was only available as an unanchored hidden text element, so the required status and reason checks could not be completed.
Update the checkpoint to use a stable result container or accessible label, and wait for that container before asserting both the Dangerous status and the imitation reason.

tests.name: Shield refuses to save a look-alike of a saved person
tests.summary:
Filled the Add someone form with the name “Ada new” and the provided wallet address, then selected “Save person.”
The page reported that the address was not saved because it looked like Ada’s saved address but was not an exact match.
“Ada new” was not added to the Your people list.

tests.name: Paying a name that is both a saved person and another user asks who you meant
tests.summary:
The requested $5 coffee payment to Semi was entered.
After selecting Pay $5.00, the page asked which Semi was intended and showed both the saved contact and the @semi user options.
Your contact Semi was selected.
The payment was completed, with confirmation that $5.00 was sent to Semi.

tests.name: The Android page offers the app install and a safe keyboard download
tests.summary:
Opened the requested Mlyfo web manifest page, which led to Mlyfo’s Android page.
Confirmed the Android page includes the “Mlyfo on your Android phone” heading, a “Download the keyboard” button, and Chrome installation guidance.
Confirmed the page states that internet is the keyboard’s only permission, keystrokes never leave the phone, and provides a SHA-256 download fingerprint.
Confirmed the manifest identifies the app as “Mlyfo” with a standalone display mode.

tests.name: The Android page offers the app install and a safe keyboard download
